packageRules.description: The example app's runtime versions are dictated by the installed Expo SDK, and expo-doctor fails the build when they drift. Refresh the lockfile inside the declared ranges, never widen them. SDK jumps are done by hand.
Metro is pinned to whatever line React Native ships with, same reason.

react-test-renderer has to match the installed react exactly or @testing-library/react-native refuses to run the suite. React's version comes from the Expo SDK, so this one moves by hand alongside it.

packages/modal builds and tests against the same react-native the example app runs, which the Expo SDK dictates. Bumping it on its own installs a second copy and expo-doctor fails on the duplicate. Moves by hand with the SDK.
typescript-eslint ships @typescript-eslint/eslint-plugin and /parser, and ESLint throws `Cannot redefine plugin` if a separate copy of the plugin ends up in the tree. Bump them together.
